newsitem.title: USA: Pricey West Coast crudes draw more Canada imports.
newsitem.headline: Pricey West Coast crudes draw more Canada imports.

text.p: High prices for U.S. West Coast crude oil are drawing greater-than-expected volumes of Canadian imports this month, industry sources said.

"Usually, it's declining volumes into Washington State rather than increasing," said Rich Ballantyne, manager of oil movement on Trans Mountain Pipe Line Inc, the main artery between U.S. Northwest refiners and Canada.
March shipments of Canadian crude are expected to reach 105,000 barrels-per-day on Trans Mountain Pipe Line, a 31 percent increase over earlier forecasts of 72,000 bpd, Ballantyne said.
"It's surprisingly high," said one oil trader.
Ballantyne and other traders assumed imports West would fall due to expansions of pipelines going east from Canada.

"In reality, Alaska North Slope (ANS) closed so close to West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the price paid by West Coast refiners matched or exceeded the price going east," Ballantyne said, referring to Canadian prices.
ANS -- priced at a discount to WTI -- has reached its highest value relative to bellwether grade since early 1996.
Buyers of lighter Canadian grades are stuck paying up to $1.25 a barrel over WTI in the current market.
On the supply side, Canadian producers have been able to divert supplies West because U.S. Midwest refiners, heavy Canadian buyers, are currently buying many overseas crudes.
Ballantyne said line-fill needed for a new pipeline and the maintenance shutdown of a large synthetic crude plant in Canada will squeeze supplies to the West Coast next month.
"I think the number will decrease, but I don't know to what level," he said.
That has some refiners in the Pacific Northwest looking to buy more overseas crude to contain ANS prices, which a year-ago rose rose to -$0.60 under WTI.
"They may start to bring in light (crude) from elsewhere," said a trader for a California refiner.
ANS is currently priced at $0.90 under WTI.
Shell Oil, which operates a large refinery in Washington state, has discussed buying Far East cargoes with other West Coast oil companies, California traders say.
